ideas.risks: The rounding-to-low-levels dominance may fail at a strict-crossing boundary, the old-high subtraction S_j=V^*_{s_j}-hH may miss a comparator regime, or intermediate zero horizons may create constraints not represented by the low horizons.
ideas.summary: Prove or disprove the solver's full-to-reduced LP reduction for one unequal-low drought. Start from the accepted finite-prefix D_n primal in the formal left-limit model, partition quote coordinates into protected old-high, useful segment, and final-only classes, justify the action menu L union {h}, derive the low-horizon constraints and final-high debt constraint, and show all intermediate zero horizons are dominated by the latest low constraint.
ideas.title: Audit Unequal-Low LP Reduction
ideas.why_promising: This is the immediate bottleneck in iteration 18. A clean proof promotes the candidate LP to an accepted local theorem; a failure gives a precise counterexample to the solver attempt.

ideas.risks: The displayed dual may be only the dual of the reduced LP, not of the full finite-prefix LP; dual mass on intermediate horizons could improve the certificate; low-level menus may need running maxima not included in L.
ideas.summary: Attack the same theorem from the finite-prefix dual. Restrict dual support to low horizons and the final high, compute the per-segment support terms, and verify that they match the solver's psi_i expression. Then ask whether any omitted horizon can increase the full dual objective in one-drought paths.
ideas.title: Dualize The Drought LP
ideas.why_promising: The solver's dual formula is compact and may be the cleanest route to a lower bound. It also directly checks the final-debt term and the S_j normalization.

ideas.risks: The reduced LP may be a generic piecewise-linear program with no clean pooling law; nonmonotone lows can destroy the chain structure that PAVA relies on; active-set formulas may become more complex than useful.
ideas.summary: Assuming the reduced LP is exact, derive a pooling, PAVA-like, or nested-resource-allocation algorithm from its dual. Use complementary slackness to identify active low constraints, active segment levels c, and the beta/alpha tradeoff between low payoff and final high debt. Regression-test on two- and three-low examples, including nonmonotone low sequences.
ideas.title: Pooling Rule For Unequal Lows
ideas.why_promising: A structural solver would turn the local LP into a usable surplus/debt rule and might reveal the right state variable for repeated droughts.

ideas.risks: Finite experiments may pass without yielding insight; numerical LP tolerances can hide strict-crossing or left-limit issues; exhaustive search grows quickly with path length and alphabet size.
ideas.summary: Build a small exact finite-prefix LP regression suite. For grids of lows such as {0.25,0.5,0.75}, enumerate one-drought paths with small M, N_i, L, compute D_n from LB-031, compute the proposed reduced LP, and compare primal/dual certificates. Prioritize minimal failing examples, then extend to repeated droughts.
ideas.title: Exact LP Regression Suite
ideas.why_promising: This gives a precise independent check of the solver's proposed reduction and can quickly find the first missing constraint or indexing error.

ideas.risks: Single-drought formulas may not compose; the necessary state may be a high-dimensional vector of level-specific debts; experiments may only show dilution without a theorem.
ideas.summary: Study two or more unequal-low droughts sharing future highs. Compare the full finite-prefix value with sums or compositions of the single-drought LP. Track how low-level quote mass creates persistent high debt and whether debt can be summarized by level, by segment, or by a scalar workload.
ideas.title: Repeated-Drought High Debt
ideas.why_promising: The notes identify repeated droughts and cumulative high debt as the main remaining route toward the D_n=o(n) gluing problem. This direction tests whether the new local LP is composable.

ideas.risks: The augmented certificate may become tautological or too close to the full D_n dual; separated-block examples already show naive boundary charging fails, so a useful localization theorem needs extra structure.
ideas.summary: Define a boundary-augmented prefix LP that keeps late shadow thresholds in the local certificate. Use the one-drought LP as a model: lows are local horizons, the resolving high is a shadow objective creating debt. Explore whether repeated augmented boundary defects either force comparable-scale D_n or are exactly absorbed by later quote opportunities.
ideas.title: Boundary-Augmented Localization
ideas.why_promising: This addresses the known failure of direct dual localization while preserving the information that made separated and drought examples analyzable.
